postings.title: Product Designer
postings.description:
About Ande


Ande makes Corporate Entertainment Effortless. Marketing, sales, EAs and workplace teams use Ande’s AI to book client dinners, sports suites, catering, merch and more. Policies, spend and logistics are managed in one place, with one vendor.

Over 60 enterprises run their entertainment on Ande, with $400 million+ in annual entertainment spend flowing through a network of 93,000 entertainment providers across 90+ cities. Ande has raised $52 million+ in seed and Series A funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, Duration Ventures and Sierra Ventures, with participation from Bain Capital Ventures.





About the Role
We're looking for a Product Designer to join our growing design team. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment and is excited to grow their ownership and craft across meaningful product areas. This is a hands-on role for someone who is curious, comfortable with ambiguity, and energized by building, shipping, and iterating.

What You'll Do

 - Own the end-to-end design for defined features and product areas, from problem framing through execution, launch, and iteration

 - Work upstream when needed, helping define what to build and why, not just designing a solution once the problem is handed to you

 - Quickly explore and design product ideas, from rough concepts and flows to high-fidelity UI and interactive prototypes

 - Translate complex, AI-driven, data-heavy, or workflow-oriented problems into clear, intuitive user journeys

 - Proactively identify UX issues and experience gaps, and bring concrete proposals, written or visual, to the team

 - Apply excellent visual design craft (typography, layout, spacing, and color) to produce interfaces that are both beautiful and usable

 - Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Operations, contributing to roadmap discussions and trade-off decisions

 - Participate in user research and synthesis to better understand enterprise users, real-world workflows, and operational constraints

 - Use and contribute to our design system, prioritizing speed, consistency, and usability

 - Actively use AI tools throughout your daily workflow, for writing, research synthesis, ideation, prototyping, and rapid iteration

What We're Looking For

 - 2-4 years of experience in UX or Product Design, ideally within B2B, enterprise SaaS, or complex workflow-driven products

 - Experience contributing to end-to-end design initiatives and shipping real product

 - Strong UX fundamentals and the ability to work through ambiguous problems with structure and clarity

 - Strong visual judgment and taste; you know when something is good enough and when it isn't, and you can articulate why

 - The ability to clearly explain and defend your design decisions to cross-functional partners, connecting them to user needs

 - The ability to communicate design thinking beyond pixels; you can write a clear problem statement, annotate a flow, or put together a lightweight brief when the work calls for it

 - Experience designing for multi-step processes or workflow-driven products

 - Growing sense of agency: you take initiative and ask good questions

 - Proficiency with modern design tools (e.g., Figma, Claude Code) and comfort working at both strategic and tactical levels

 - Interest in designing AI-powered products and comfort in AI-native, fast-feedback environments

Bonus Points

 - Experience in a startup or similarly fast-paced environment

 - Experience designing for iOS native mobile

 - Experience in travel, expense management, fintech, or adjacent enterprise platforms

 - Experience designing AI-powered or AI-assisted product experiences

 - Regular use of AI tools to support UX work

 - Some front-end literacy or comfort thinking in components and systems

Equal Employment Opportunity


Ande is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and will consider all applicants for employment without regard to any legally protected status

postings.title: Product Manager, Payments
postings.description:
About Ande


Ande makes Corporate Entertainment Effortless. Marketing, sales, EAs and workplace teams use Ande’s AI to book client dinners, sports suites, catering, merch and more. Policies, spend and logistics are managed in one place, with one vendor.

Over 60 enterprises run their entertainment on Ande, with $400 million+ in annual entertainment spend flowing through a network of 93,000 entertainment providers across 90+ cities. Ande has raised $52 million+ in seed and Series A funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, Duration Ventures and Sierra Ventures, with participation from Bain Capital Ventures.



About the Role
We're building the platform for corporate entertainment: the dinners, events, and client experiences where business actually happens. It's a massive market that still runs largely on manual processes, and we're bringing it onto software for the first time. Payments sits at the heart of that: it's how money moves through everything we do, and where the value we create becomes real. We're looking for a PM to own Ande's payments solutions for our suppliers: the platform that moves money through everything we do, and the payment and financial tools built on top of it. Your focus will be the workflows that serve our suppliers, getting paid reliably, managing receivables, and running smooth payment operations. This is the kind of product work where every improvement is felt immediately: money arrives faster, operations get lighter, and the businesses we serve notice. You'll own the roadmap, ship across multiple surfaces, and drive adoption, with real money movement from day one. AI isn't a feature we bolted on, it's the foundation of our product and how we run the company: we automate what can be automated so people spend their time on judgment, not busywork. As a PM here, you'll prototype ideas yourself, get answers from data without waiting on anyone, and ship faster than you're probably used to.


What You'll Do

 - Own product strategy and roadmap for our payments platform, with a focus on supplier-facing workflows

 - Own the payment experiences our suppliers touch, from getting paid to understanding their money

 - Own payment partner and banking integrations, the rails everything else runs on

 - Own the internal tooling behind our payment operations, supporting the team that keeps payouts, reconciliation, and exceptions running smoothly

 - Own new financial product initiatives: receivables, analytics, and whatever we discover our customers need next

 - Define, prioritize, and execute the roadmap for our payments products

 - Own relationships with payment and banking partners alongside our finance and operations stakeholders

 - Partner with engineering and design to ship high-quality features at startup speed

 - Work directly with Operations, Finance, Customer Success, and Sales, sitting at the intersection of product and the business

 - Translate customer needs into scalable product solutions

 - Drive prioritization using data, customer feedback, and business objectives

What We're Looking For

 - 5+ years of Product Management experience

 - Experience building payments, fintech, marketplace, or financial products

 - Strong technical aptitude and ability to work closely with engineering teams

 - Experience partnering across product, operations, finance, and go-to-market teams

 - High agency; you spot what matters, take ownership, and run without waiting for permission

 - Strong communication, prioritization, and problem-solving skills

Bonus Points

 - Experience with payment processing, merchant acquiring, payment facilitation, payouts, or receivables

 - Experience building for small businesses or operators; you know what "simple" has to mean for a busy user

 - Experience with marketplace payment flows

 - Exposure to payment regulations or financial compliance requirements


Why This Role Matters
Own the products that move real money for real businesses, with company-wide visibility and immediate, tangible impact. Work directly with founders and leadership on strategy and execution. Small team, high ownership: your decisions ship, fast. Build the payments backbone of a category-defining company, early enough that your fingerprints are on everything.

postings.title: Product Manager, AI
postings.description:
About Ande


Ande makes Corporate Entertainment Effortless. Marketing, sales, EAs and workplace teams use Ande’s AI to book client dinners, sports suites, catering, merch and more. Policies, spend and logistics are managed in one place, with one vendor.

Over 60 enterprises run their entertainment on Ande, with $400 million+ in annual entertainment spend flowing through a network of 93,000 entertainment providers across 90+ cities. Ande has raised $52 million+ in seed and Series A funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, Duration Ventures and Sierra Ventures, with participation from Bain Capital Ventures.



About the Role
Corporate teams spend billions every year on business entertainment, dinners, events, client experiences, and almost none of it runs through purpose-built software. At the center of our platform are AI agents that do real work for our customers: agents that carry multi-step, high-stakes workflows through to completion, with real money and real relationships on the line. We're looking for a PM to own these agentic experiences. There's no established playbook for this work; the patterns for running agents in production are being figured out in real time, by a small number of teams, and we're one of the teams doing the inventing. You'll own how our agents behave, how their quality is measured and improved, and how the system earns the trust to take on more. AI isn't a feature we bolted on, it's the foundation of our product and how we run the company: we automate what can be automated so people spend their time on judgment, not busywork. As a PM here, you'll prototype ideas yourself, get answers from data without waiting on anyone, and ship faster than you're probably used to.



What You'll Do

 - Own the end-to-end experience our customers have with our AI agents, from first interaction to completed outcome

 - Own agent quality as a product: evaluation frameworks, review loops, and the metrics that define "good" for a production agent

 - Own the division of labor between agents and people, where automation earns more autonomy, and where human judgment stays in the workflow

 - Own the improvement engine: the feedback loops and mechanisms that make agents measurably better every week, at growing volume

 - Define, prioritize, and execute the roadmap for our agentic product experiences

 - Go deep in the mechanics: prompt and context engineering, evals, failure analysis; you'll read transcripts, find patterns, and turn them into product decisions

 - Partner with engineering to ship improvements fast, and build the tooling that makes quality visible and measurable

 - Work closely with the operations teams whose workflows interlock with the agents; they're part of your product surface

 - Coordinate with PMs across the product group, since the agents touch nearly every part of the customer journey

 - Track the frontier: new patterns, research, and techniques emerge weekly in this space, and part of your job is knowing what's real, what's noise, and what we should try next
   
   

What We're Looking For

 - 5+ years of Product Management experience, including hands-on work shipping agentic workflows

 - Fluency in the patterns of production agentic systems, things like escalation and handoff design, guardrails, human-in-the-loop, feedback loops, and eval-driven development, and the judgment to know which pattern fits which problem

 - A habit of staying at the edge: this field reinvents itself every few months, and you're the kind of person who's already tried the new technique before most people have heard of it

 - Systems thinking; you see the agent, the people around it, the feedback loops, and the failure modes as one system, and you design for the whole

 - An empirical mindset; you'd rather read fifty transcripts than debate a hypothesis, and you know quality is measured, not assumed

 - Strong technical fluency, comfortable with prompt and context engineering, and able to work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers on agent architecture

 - High agency; you spot what matters, take ownership, and run without waiting for permission
   
   

Bonus Points

 - You've operated an agentic product in production, with real users and real consequences; you know what breaks at volume that demos never show

 - You've built evaluation systems or quality frameworks for non-deterministic products

 - Experience in marketplaces or products mediating between two parties

 - You write, speak, or build in public about agentic systems, or you're active in the communities where this craft is developing
   
   

Why This Role Matters
 Own the most visible, customer-facing part of what we do, and problems most PMs won't get to touch for years. Work directly with founders and leadership on strategy and execution. Small team, high ownership: your decisions ship, fast. Help define how agentic products get built, at a company where that's the whole point, early enough that your fingerprints are on everything.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and will consider all applicants for employment without regard to any legally protected status

That's the concierge and its team of subagents that take a request from one sentence ("dinner for 12 with the Acme team next Thursday, somewhere private") to a confirmed, paid, on-policy booking. Along the way they source venues, compare options, email the venue and negotiate terms, and handle every change after that.

This is not a chatbot or a demo. The agent acts on real money, on behalf of real executives, with real venues on the other end of the thread. It runs in production today for reservations and private dining. Our strategy depends on carrying more of the work with every request: more kinds of entertainment, more cities, more of the workflow, without growing headcount to match. You will set how we get there.



What You'll Do

 - Own the agent system. Ande runs on a root concierge agent with specialist subagents for sourcing, comparison, and venue coordination, on a self-hosted agent harness behind queued turn workers. You’ll own its architecture, model choices, and upgrade path, and make sure it holds up under latency budgets, provider failover, and real-world load.

 - Build tools the agent can trust. The agent has about 75 typed capabilities that let it search, hold, book, pay, and message. Each one runs as the acting user and respects who they’re acting for, such as an assistant booking on behalf of an executive. Consequential actions become proposals that the booker confirms. You’ll decide what the agent is allowed to do, and how to make it safe.

 - Make evals the gate for every change. You’ll build scenario suites, graders, and LLM judges calibrated against human labels. They replay from recorded runs on every PR and run in full nightly. Your goal is evals trustworthy enough that a model upgrade or prompt change can ship on the strength of the number alone, and cheap enough to run all the time.

 - Power venue correspondence. Our agent negotiates with venues over email. It reads replies, pulls out offers, minimums, deadlines, and payment requests, and knows when to push, when to wait, and when to hand off to a person. You’ll make sure all of it is resistant to anything a third party writes into a thread.

 - Build memory and the supply learning loop. You’ll shape what the agent remembers about a company, its people, and its venues, with clear rules on what’s shared and what stays private. You’ll also build the loop that turns every venue conversation into structured supply data, like which room actually fits 14 or what a venue will do on a Tuesday, so each recommendation is better than the last.

 - Ship fast, reliable judgments. You’ll build typed classifiers for consent, triage, ranking, and urgency. Each has labeled thresholds, a timeout, and a fallback, and each rolls out from shadow mode to live.

 - Set the bar for building with AI. You’ll define how Ande builds with AI: agent behavior as versioned config, product teammates proposing changes through evals, and AI coding agents as the default way the team ships. You’ll mentor engineers and partner closely with our AI product manager.



What We’re Looking For

 - Education and experience: a degree in Computer Science or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. You have 5+ years building production software, including 2+ years shipping LLM agents to real customers (tool use, multi-step planning, structured outputs, long-running conversations).

 - Production evals: you’ve owned evals in production, from writing them to finding failure modes in real traffic and improving quality turn by turn.

 - Systems engineering: strong TypeScript and backend skills, including queues, concurrency, idempotency, and how distributed systems fail.

 - Sound judgment: you know where a model belongs and where deterministic code does, and you have the discipline to make agent actions safe, auditable, and reversible.

 - AI-native workflow: you use AI coding agents every day. Our codebase is built to be worked on by them, and we expect you to raise that bar.

 - Clear communication: you can explain agent behavior and trade-offs to product, operations, and customers.



Bonus Points

 - You've been a founding or early engineer and know how to balance craft, ownership and speed.

 - You've built agent harnesses, orchestration layers or tool brokers, not just prompts.

 - Experience with search, ranking or recommendation systems.

 - Experience with marketplaces, booking or payments, where a wrong action costs money.

 - Experience defending agents against prompt injection from untrusted content.



Why This Role Matters

The Ande Agent is how we scale. Every request it handles end to end is work we don’t have to hire for, so how far it can take us depends on the person who owns its intelligence.

The stakes are real. The agent moves real money for executives and negotiates directly with venues, so a mistake costs customers money and costs us venue relationships. Every venue conversation also makes the agent smarter. That learning loop is an advantage competitors can’t easily copy.

This isn’t an AI feature bolted onto a product. The agent is the product, and you’ll own how it thinks.



This is an in-office position (4 days/week) in New York City

postings.title: Product Marketing Lead
postings.description:
About Ande


Ande makes Corporate Entertainment Effortless. Marketing, sales, EAs and workplace teams use Ande’s AI to book client dinners, sports suites, catering, merch and more. Policies, spend and logistics are managed in one place, with one vendor.

Over 60 enterprises run their entertainment on Ande, with $400 million+ in annual entertainment spend flowing through a network of 93,000 entertainment providers across 90+ cities. Ande has raised $52 million+ in seed and Series A funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, Duration Ventures and Sierra Ventures, with participation from Bain Capital Ventures.



We're hiring our first Product Marketing Lead to own how Ande's products are launched, adopted and used. You'll report to the VP of Marketing.

Ande ships fast, across two product suites for two very different audiences:

 - Enterprise: an AI-native operating system for corporate entertainment where users can book dining, catering, sports, merch and experiences and manage the event end to end (including payment).

 - Hospitality and vendors: AI agents that capture and convert corporate demand for restaurants and entertainment partners.

This role owns two main motions:

 1. New product launches and market education on the product, ie. evangelizing the depth and breath of what you can do on Ande for both enterprises and vendors.

 2. What happens after signup: getting users to discover, adopt and keep booking through Ande.

Expect to prioritize ruthlessly and shape how the product marketing team grows from here.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Launch products, end to end

 - Own positioning, messaging and go-to-market for new products and features across the enterprise and hospitality suites.

 - Plan launches across internal and external channels: in-product prompts, post-sales outreach, earned and owned media, newsletters and guest spots on partner platforms.

 - Use beta and advisory board programs to launch with case studies, testimonials and customer voices already in hand.

Drive in-product adoption and usage growth

 - Own the product experience after customer acquisition.

 - Own the post-signup journey: activation, first booking, repeat usage and expansion to new teams inside existing accounts, working closely with the CSM team.

 - Own onboarding and education sequences for newly activated users, plus the in-product announcements and notifications that move users beyond email newsletters.

 - Map the personas already in our customer base (field marketers, EAs, workplace experience, sales) and work with product to bring each the features that matter to them.

 - Run timely, revenue-driving pushes around seasonal moments such as major sporting events, live events and holiday gifting.

 - Run usage promos, campaigns and pilots for existing customers, working with the email channel owner to ship them, then measure and iterate.

Enable sales, customer success and the services team

 - Give GTM and post-sales teams what they need at every stage: demos, one-pagers, objection handling, case studies and persona-mapped email templates.

 - Run regular enablement on new features and on our growing partner catalog across ticketing, catering and gifting.

Educate the market and be the face of what's new

 - Be the on-camera face and voice of product updates on social media and through podcast-style videos, demo videos, sizzle reels and educational webinars.

 - Turn platform data into stories and content, like annual recaps for customers and partners.

 - Explain a category that overlaps many tools but is done end to end by no one, to marketers, EAs, workplace teams, procurement and finance.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7+ years in B2B product marketing, ideally including building the function from scratch at an early-stage company.

 - Experience marketing to business buyers such as marketers, operations or finance, not only to developers or IT.

 - A track record in full-funnel and bottom-of-funnel work: adoption, self-serve education, retention and expansion, not just messaging.

 - Comfort on camera and in front of an audience. You'll host videos and webinars, not only script them, and you're a strong written and spoken communicator.

 - An analytical approach: you define funnel metrics, read the data and change course based on it.

 - Hands-on sales and customer success enablement experience.

 - Judgment to prioritize hard when every team wants something, and the drive to execute what you recommend.

 - Fluency with AI tools in your own workflow, from content production to documentation.

Bonus points

 - Product-led growth or in-app lifecycle marketing experience.

 - Experience with two-sided marketplaces, or marketing to both enterprise buyers and SMB operators.

 - Background in events, field marketing, hospitality, travel or spend management.

 - You've run a customer advisory board, beta program or product roadmapping workshops.

 - A finance or analytics background.

 - You're the person your team asks to find the dinner spot.
